mainEntity.name: How much does a Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,500, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded hybrid components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge £5,000-£7,000+ for the same replacement. Used engines are a budget alternative, starting from around £1,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of hybrid system failure in a Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early detection of hybrid faults can prevent catastrophic damage to your Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD powertrain. Signs include illumination of the Check Hybrid System or engine management warning light, the vehicle entering limp mode or losing power during acceleration, and unusual whining noises from the inverter or visible coolant leaks beneath the vehicle. If you notice these symptoms, get your Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely. The Honda Accord Hybrid retains exceptionally strong market values, typically ranging from £12,000 to £22,000. A full rebuilt engine replacement (£3,500-£5,000) represents a small fraction of the vehicle's total worth. Investing in a warrantied, reconditioned unit preserves the car's performance and resale value far better than a cheap, unverified used engine.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct LFA-H4 hybrid powertrain unit, nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, hybrid system calibration, fluid top-up, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the LFA-H4 and standard Accord engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The LFA-H4 is a dedicated hybrid powertrain specific to the Accord i-MMD, combining a 2.0L Atkinson-cycle petrol engine with dual electric motors and a power control unit (PCU). Unlike standard K-series or R-series petrol engines, the LFA-H4 is designed for seamless electric-to-petrol transitions. It requires specialist hybrid diagnostic equipment and calibrated replacement units to ensure the high-voltage systems communicate correctly with the vehicle's ECU.

historyTimeline.h2: Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Hybrid i-MMD (Intelligent Multi-Mode Drive) was introduced to the Honda Accord lineup, it brought advanced electrification to the executive saloon, combining a highly efficient Atkinson-cycle petrol engine with dual electric motors for seamless, responsive performance.

milestones.description: LFA-H4 (215 PS combined) introduced in the 10th generation Honda Accord Hybrid, replacing the previous generation's hybrid system with a more robust, direct-drive focused i-MMD architecture.
Minor software and emissions refinements to the i-MMD system, maintaining the LFA-H4 powertrain as the sole hybrid offering until the model's eventual discontinuation in the UK market.

commonProblems.h2: Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD is renowned for its reliability, but the complexity of its dual-motor and inverter system introduces specific failure points. The LFA-H4 code dominates replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Inverter Cooling System Leaks & High-Voltage Battery Degradation
problems.h4: Inverter Cooling System Leaks & High-Voltage Battery Degradation
problems.rootCause: The inverter coolant pump or associated seals can degrade over time, leading to coolant ingress or overheating of the power control unit (PCU). If ignored, this may trigger hybrid system shutdowns or require full powertrain replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inverter coolant pump replacement and full system flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before the PCU or battery modules sustain heat damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if the PCU has failed or severe hybrid system degradation has occurred.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD (2018-2022) is currently valued between £12,000 and £22,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Given the Accord Hybrid's strong retained value, a full rebuilt replacement (£3,500-£5,000) represents a highly viable and financially sound investment to preserve the car's performance and resale value.
problems.recommendation: For a Honda Accord Hybrid i-MMD showing early inverter cooling warnings, targeted component repair is the most financially sensible route. However, if the vehicle has suffered catastrophic PCU failure or severe hybrid system degradation, a reconditioned or rebuilt LFA-H4 unit is the most reliable long-term solution to protect your investment.
